name: paired_credit_effect
caption: Final designated-holdout performance differences from the equally trained 0% credit control. Large points average paired dataset effects after five-fold and training-seed averaging; intervals are nominal 95% paired-dataset bootstrap intervals and small markers show seed means. Positive ROC-AUC or R² and negative log-loss or CRPS differences favor treatment.

name: per_dataset_control_gap
caption: Final performance difference from the matched 0% control for every designated-holdout credit dataset and mixture, averaging five folds and three training seeds within each dataset. The diverging scale is centered on zero; positive ROC-AUC or R² differences favor the credit mixture.

name: credit_generality_frontier
caption: Final mean credit performance difference against native-OOD performance difference for each credit mixture, relative to the equally trained 0% control. Horizontal and vertical bars are separate nominal 95% paired-dataset bootstrap intervals; small marks show paired training-seed effects. Higher ROC-AUC or R² is better on both axes; zero lines indicate no difference.

name: conditional_component_effects
caption: Final designated-holdout metric differences for five component removals from the full 50% prior package, with matched training seeds and five folds. Large points show mean paired-dataset effects, bars show nominal 95% dataset-bootstrap intervals, and small markers show training-seed means. Negative ROC-AUC or R² and positive log-loss or CRPS differences indicate deterioration after removal.

name: observed_predicted_endpoint_mass
caption: Portfolio-average predicted versus observed mass near full recovery (loss 0) and total loss (loss 1) for designated-holdout LGD datasets. Each mark is a dataset/training-seed mean over five folds; colors and shapes distinguish credit mixtures and released TabICLv2. The diagonal marks aggregate agreement. Endpoint tolerance is 1e-4; predictive masses use the 99-level quantile approximation. This is not conditional calibration.
